name: pdk-pyfunctional-pipeline
instr:
Our nightly job loads the carrier's shipment feed into SQLite with PyFunctional, one call per daily file, like `seq.jsonl(path).to_sqlite3(db_path, "shipments")`. Since the carrier moved to a new export system the job keeps breaking. Three days of the new feed are in /data/shipments/; could you find what's wrong and fix it?

Every daily file has to load, in any order, into the table the earlier days made. With a table name and dict or namedtuple records, `to_sqlite3` should create a missing table and add a column, named exactly like the field, for every field the table lacks. A record without a field reads NULL there. In columns made this way, every str, int, float and None value must come back from `seq.sqlite3` with the same type and value. When the table has a primary key, a record whose key is already there replaces that row.

A call that fails part way (a value SQLite can't store, a line cut short, the sequence raising) must raise and leave the database as it was, even if the caller commits afterwards. Paths, connections and cursors should all work, with table names or INSERT statements, and a successful call is committed. Backfills run several calls at once, in separate processes on one database file; each must succeed and leave the same table as running them one after another.

The existing tests in /app/functional/test must keep passing, and pylint, black and mypy must stay clean on /app/functional. There's no network; dev tools are in /opt/venv.
